draft.body:
Dear Professor Claire Zimmerman,

Your profile connects The Costs of Architecture with industrial architecture and labour (https://www.daniels.utoronto.ca/people/core-faculty/claire-zimmerman). That offers a useful test for a proposed convenience whose costs may fall on reception staff.

I’m developing Proxy Society, an architecture research project on AI agents and robots acting for absent people under limited, revocable mandates. Could you advise which architectural history or labour question would make this more than a service demonstration, and whether that framing could fit the ALD PhD?

Best regards,
Kris Haamer

draft.body:
Dear Professor John Harwood,

The Interface: IBM and the Transformation of Corporate Design places architecture alongside technology and business in your profile (https://www.daniels.utoronto.ca/people/core-faculty/john-harwood). I want to examine that relationship at a smaller institutional threshold.

I’m developing Proxy Society, an architecture research project on AI agents and robots acting for absent people under limited, revocable mandates. I would compare a civic counter with a visible mandate-and-revocation surface against one controlled through a concealed back office. Both retain staffed appeal and personal entry. Historical cases and drawings would trace how an interface transfers authority from a person to an institution.

Could you suggest an institutional precedent that would challenge this comparison, and advise whether the historical argument could support an ALD doctoral proposal?

Best regards,
Kris Haamer

Dear Professor Zach Blas,

Your profile describes CULTUS and Facial Weaponization Suite as interventions into computational power (https://www.daniels.utoronto.ca/people/core-faculty/zach-blas). They sharpen the problem of making delegation optional when institutions decide what counts as a person.

I’m developing Proxy Society, an architecture research project on AI agents and robots acting for absent people under limited, revocable mandates. I would stage two civic thresholds: one asks a proxy to present biometric proof; the other permits a limited mandate and a human challenge without biometric enrollment. Both preserve personal arrival and staying. Film and spatial mockups would make refusal, cancellation and hidden classification visible before considering any deployment.

Could you identify where this comparison still reproduces the power it claims to question, and whether critical installation could anchor an ALD doctoral contribution?
